label: Bible Study
prompt: What? know ye not that your body is the _____ of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?
verse: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?
note: Paul's reminder to Corinth — the body is a dwelling place, not a rental to trash.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the _____.
verse: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
note: Weeping gets the night shift; joy clocks in at dawn. The psalmist knows which one has the longer contract.

label: Sunday School
prompt: The _____ also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.
verse: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.
note: Everyone remembers 'the lion shall lie down with the lamb,' but the KJV pairs the lamb with the wolf.

label: Deep Water
prompt: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a _____ of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
verse: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
note: The charter of Christian apologetics — the Greek for 'answer' is apologia, a reasoned defense, offered with meekness.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the _____.
verse: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
note: 'Kick against the pricks' — an ox kicking the farmer's goad, hurting only itself. Saul was the ox.
